title: Pulling the maintenance lever crashes every signed-in user: the takeover screen only renders for visitors with no cookies
what: The tenant layout's first act is `const [systemMode, impersonation] = await Promise.all([currentSystemMode(slug), currentImpersonation()])`, and only then checks `isTakeoverMode`. Two independent bugs make the takeover unreachable: (a) `currentImpersonation()` rethrows anything that is not a 401/403 (impersonation.ts:32), so on a 5xx or a network failure the `Promise.all` rejects before the takeover branch is evaluated; (b) `currentSystemMode()` returns the hard-coded `out_of_order` mode only for an `ApiError` — a raw fetch rejection (API process down, DNS gone, connection refused: the most common outage) falls to `return NORMAL` at system-mode.ts:53. So the branded maintenance/outage screen, its `illustrations/outage` asset and the `system.maintenance.*` / `system.outOfOrder.*` catalogue entries are dead code in exactly the situation they were written for.
impact: The takeover works ONLY for anonymous visitors. Every librarian who has ever signed in carries a cookie, so a planned maintenance window — and every unplanned outage — hands them a bare English Next.js crash page instead of the branded Greek maintenance screen. Executed: with cookie -> 500, without cookie -> 200 + Greek takeover. Operationally this means the maintenance feature has never worked for the population it exists for.
evidence: RAN both outage shapes against the production build. (1) API refused (ECONNREFUSED): `/el/t/demo -> 500`, and the RSC payload shows the layout error `6:E{"digest":"3227098399"}` — no takeover markup. (2) API answering 503 to everything (a Node stub returning `{statusCode:503,message:'upstream down'}`): `/el/t/demo -> 500`, log `⨯ Error: upstream down { status: 503, digest: '4172507616' }` — again no takeover, because `currentImpersonation()` rejected inside the same `Promise.all`.
fix: Make `currentImpersonation()` fail soft (return `null` on any error — an unreadable impersonation cookie is not an impersonation), and make `currentSystemMode()` return `out_of_order` for a non-`ApiError` rejection too, since 'cannot reach the control plane at all' is a stronger outage signal than a 5xx. Resolve the system mode before, not alongside, the impersonation probe.
verification: EXECUTED, and the finding is stronger than written. Read apps/web/lib/impersonation.ts:32 (rethrows anything not 401/403) and lib/system-mode.ts:53 (non-ApiError -> NORMAL): both mechanisms are exactly as described. Then re-ran the whole thing against the existing production build (apps/web/.next, BUILD_ID -eh04V7H-q4KJH3WJ5n38) with `next start -p 3397` pointed at a stub API that returns 200 + mode=maintenance on /system-mode/current and 503 on everything else — i.e. a DELIBERATE, PLANNED maintenance window, not an outage. Results: `curl -H 'Cookie: __Host-libriant_session=bogus' /el/t/demo` -> HTTP 500 with `<html id="__next_error__">`; the same URL with NO cookie -> HTTP 200 containing the Greek maintenance takeover ('συντήρηση'). Confirmed the cause is server-side: apps/api/src/system-mode/system-mode.middleware.ts ALWAYS_PASS covers /system-mode/*, /admin/*, /healthz, /readyz, /metrics, /webhooks/stripe and /apply — it does NOT cover /support/impersonation/me, so that endpoint 503s during maintenance, currentImpersonation() rethrows, and the Promise.all in layout.tsx:52 rejects before the takeover branch is reached. So the maintenance lever, when an operator pulls it on purpose, crashes every signed-in user instead of showing the screen built for it. Severity kept at high (no data loss, and the operator can undo it), but this is the worst finding in the dimension.

title: No error boundary anywhere in the Next app — during an API failure every authenticated route, including /login, returns a bare English 500
where: apps/web/app/ (no error.tsx / global-error.tsx exists in the whole tree); apps/web/lib/session.ts:47
what: `find apps/web/app -name 'error.tsx' -o -name 'global-error.tsx' -o -name 'loading.tsx'` returns nothing — only `apps/web/app/not-found.tsx`. `currentSession()` (session.ts:40-49) swallows 401/403/404 but rethrows every other failure, including a raw fetch rejection (API unreachable). `LoginPage` (app/[locale]/login/page.tsx:23) calls it unconditionally whenever the request carries ANY cookie, because `requestCookieHeader()` returns the whole cookie header, not just the session cookie. With no error boundary, the throw escapes to Next's DefaultGlobalError.
impact: During any API outage the librarian cannot even reach the sign-in form. They get an unstyled, unbranded, untranslated English page reading 'This page couldn't load / A server error occurred. Reload to try again.' with no Libriant branding, no Greek, no support contact and no link back. There is no route in the app that degrades gracefully — the landing page and legal pages are the only survivors.
evidence: RAN: built the app (`NODE_ENV=production pnpm --filter @libriant/web build`, succeeded) then `next start` with `API_INTERNAL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:59999` (nothing listening). With `Cookie: __Host-libriant_session=bogus`: `/el/login -> 500`, `/el/signup -> 500`, `/admin/login -> 500`, `/el/t/demo -> 500`, `/el/t/demo/loans -> 500`. Server log: `⨯ [TypeError: fetch failed] { digest: '3227098399', [cause]: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:59999 }`. The 500 body is `<html id="__next_error__">` with an empty `<body>`. READ: apps/web/node_modules/next/dist/client/components/builtin/global-error.js — `children: "This page couldn’t load"`, `message = 'A server error occurred. Reload to try again.'`.
fix: Add `apps/web/app/[locale]/error.tsx` and `apps/web/app/global-error.tsx` that render a localized, branded outage screen (reuse the `illustrations/outage` asset and the `system.outOfOrder.*` catalogue keys) with a Retry button. Separately, make `LoginPage` tolerate a failed `currentSession()`: wrap it in try/catch and render the form when the session probe fails — a login form needs no session lookup to be useful.
verification: MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION, SEVERITY CUT FROM BLOCKER. I re-ran it against the existing production build (apps/web/.next) with `next start -p 3397` pointed at a stub API returning 503: `curl -H 'Cookie: __Host-libriant_session=bogus' /el/login` -> HTTP 500, body `<!DOCTYPE html><html id="__next_error__">` with an empty body element. Confirmed there is no error.tsx or global-error.tsx anywhere under apps/web/app (only not-found.tsx), and lib/session.ts:47 rethrows everything that is not 401/403/404. But the blocker rating does not survive two facts I checked. (1) `curl /el/login` with NO cookie header -> HTTP 200, the sign-in form renders fine; requestCookieHeader() returns undefined when the request carries no cookies at all, and I confirmed the web app sets no cookies of its own (`grep -rn "cookies().set|document.cookie" apps/web` -> nothing; no Set-Cookie on /el). So a first-time visitor is unaffected; only a browser that has already signed in is. (2) The harm is a degraded error page during a state in which the product is already unusable — signing in requires the API — with no data loss and no security consequence. High, not blocker: it must not displace attention from findings that lose circulation records.

title: Every API error message is shown to Greek librarians in raw English; the translated errors.json catalogue is bypassed everywhere
where: apps/web/lib/api.ts:26-35 (ApiError.message = server text); 93 call sites render it, e.g. apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/page.tsx:39, apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/[id]/LoanActions.tsx:155
what: `ApiError` sets `message` to the API's `message` field verbatim, and the UI renders `err instanceof ApiError ? err.message : <fallback>` in 93 places. The API throws 336 exceptions (`grep -rn 'Exception(' apps/api/src | grep -v spec | wc -l` → 336), all with hardcoded English strings such as `'Member not found.'`, `'Due date must be after the checkout date — pick a later day.'`, `'Return time cannot be earlier than the checkout time.'` (apps/api/src/loans/loans.service.ts:153,161,371). Meanwhile `locales/el/errors.json` contains a complete, parameterised Greek error catalogue (13 keys, incl. `permission.denied`, `quotaExceeded.*`, `validation.*`) that is referenced from only 4 places in the entire web app — and in all 4 only as the fallback for a NON-ApiError.
impact: Every failure a Greek librarian hits in normal work — wrong due date, member already has too many loans, copy unavailable, no permission — appears as an English sentence inside an otherwise fully Greek UI. For a product sold to Greek municipal and school libraries this is the most visible quality defect in the app, and the localized copy to fix it already exists and is unused.
evidence: READ: `apps/web/lib/api.ts:30-31` `const friendly = Array.isArray(body.message) ? body.message.join(' ') : body.message; super(friendly ?? ...)`. RAN: `grep -rn 'err.message|instanceof ApiError ? err' apps/web | wc -l` → 93; `grep -rn 'Exception(' apps/api/src | grep -v spec | wc -l` → 336; `grep -rn "t('errors\." apps/web` → 4 hits, all fallbacks. READ locales/el/errors.json — 13 fully translated keys.
fix: Give every API exception a stable machine code in the body (`{ code: 'loans.dueBeforeCheckout', params: {...} }`) alongside the human message, and add a single `translateApiError(err, t)` helper in `lib/api.ts` that resolves `errors.<code>` from the catalogue and only falls back to `err.message` for unmapped codes. Route all 93 call sites through it.
verification: CONFIRMED. Read apps/web/lib/api.ts:26-34 — `super(friendly ?? ...)` does set ApiError.message to the server's English string. Re-ran the counts: `grep -rn 'instanceof ApiError ? err' apps/web` -> 90 (auditor said 93; same order of magnitude, claim stands), `grep -rn 'Exception(' apps/api/src | grep -v spec` -> 336 exactly. Spot-checked apps/api/src/loans/loans.service.ts:153 ('Due date must be after the checkout date — pick a later day.'), :159 ('Member not found.'), :371 ('Return time cannot be earlier than the checkout time.') — all hardcoded English. Read locales/el/errors.json: 13 fully translated keys, and `grep "t('errors."` returns only 4 sites, all as the non-ApiError fallback. Nothing refutes it.

title: When a circulation action fails server-side the error toast renders behind the modal's top layer — invisible and unclickable — and the modal never closes
what: In `LoanActions.call()` the success path and the offline path both call `setOpenModal(null)`, but the final `catch` branch (ApiError — 409 already returned, 403 role, 402 quota, 422 validation, renewal cap) only fires a `severity:'critical'` toast and leaves the modal open. `Modal` uses a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, which places it in the browser's **top layer** — above every z-index — and makes the rest of the document inert. The toast stack lives outside the dialog at `z-index: 9000`, so it is painted under `.lbr-modal::backdrop` (`background: #0f172a99`) and is not hit-testable.
impact: The most common circulation failure produces no visible feedback at all: the modal just sits there. The librarian presses the button again. The idempotency key is (correctly) not rotated on error, so the retry replays, but the human has no idea what went wrong or whether the book was returned. Same defect applies to every other modal that toasts on error (BookDetail, MemberDetail, BarcodeScanner, data-model editors).
evidence: RAN: served a repro built from the real `packages/ui/src/styles.css` with a `showModal()`'d `.lbr-modal` and a `.lbr-toast.lbr-toast--critical` in `.lbr-toast-stack`, then measured in the browser: `document.elementFromPoint(toastCentre)` → `"lbr-btn lbr-btn--primary lbr-btn--md"` (the modal's button), and at the toast's close-button centre → also the modal's button. Screenshot shows the toast is not visible at all behind the backdrop. READ: LoanActions.tsx:152-157 — no `setOpenModal(null)` on the ApiError path.
fix: Two changes. (1) Close the modal (or render an inline `<Banner severity="critical">` inside the modal body) before toasting on the error path — inline is better here because the librarian is mid-task. (2) Render the toast stack into the top layer as well, e.g. via CSS `position: fixed; ` plus a `popover` / a per-dialog toast outlet, so a toast can never be occluded by an open dialog.
verification: CONFIRMED by reading the real code rather than a repro. apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/[id]/LoanActions.tsx: the success path (line 111) and the offline path (line 145) both call setOpenModal(null); the final catch (lines 152-157) fires only a critical toast and never closes the modal — verified verbatim. packages/ui/src/Modal.tsx:44 calls dlg.showModal(), which puts the <dialog> in the browser TOP LAYER and makes the rest of the document inert; packages/ui/src/styles.css:589-598 puts .lbr-toast-stack at z-index 9000 in the normal layer, and :436 gives .lbr-modal::backdrop rgba(15,23,42,0.6) + blur. Top layer beats any z-index by specification, so the toast is both occluded and non-hit-testable. Also confirmed ToastProvider renders the stack as a sibling of {children} (Toast.tsx:72-74), i.e. outside every dialog. Also confirmed all three modals are mounted unconditionally at LoanActions.tsx:176-200, so this is the normal state of the page.

title: Offline circulation writes that can never succeed are deleted with a single 5-second toast and no persistent record
what: The replay loop deletes a queued action in three cases — expired (>18 h, OfflineQueueProvider.tsx:99-106), any 4xx (line 136), and after `MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS` 5xx retries — and in every case the ONLY notification is `toast.show({severity:'critical', title: ...})`. `ToastProvider` defaults `durationMs: 5000` and nothing passes an override, so the message auto-dismisses after five seconds. There is no failed-actions list, no badge, no server-side record, and `pendingCount` drops back to 0. The flush also runs on mount (line 178), so the whole batch can be dropped and announced before the librarian has looked at the screen.
impact: A librarian checks out ten books during a Friday-afternoon network cut, shuts the laptop, and opens it Monday. Every entry is now older than 18 h, so on mount all ten are deleted unreplayed with ten stacked toasts that vanish in five seconds. Ten books are physically out of the library and the system says they are on the shelf. The same silent loss happens for any single action the server rejects with a 4xx. The 18-hour expiry itself is a sound decision (it protects against double-applying past the server's idempotency window) — the defect is that its output is a disappearing toast instead of a durable, actionable list.
evidence: READ: OfflineQueueProvider.tsx:99-106 (`await removeQueued(action.id); ctx.current.toast.show({severity:'critical', title: t('loans.queue.expired', ...)})`) and :136-141 (same shape for `syncFailed`). READ: Toast.tsx:57 `const item: ToastItem = { id, durationMs: 5000, ...toast };` — OfflineQueueProvider passes no `durationMs`. `grep -rn 'loans.queue' apps/web` shows every queue outcome is toast-only; there is no queue/history screen anywhere in `app/[locale]/t/[slug]/`.
fix: Move dropped entries to a `failed` IndexedDB store instead of deleting them, and surface them in a persistent, dismissible panel in the tenant shell ("3 offline actions could not be saved — review") listing book, member, action and time, with a one-click 'redo this manually' deep link. Make the drop toasts sticky (`durationMs: null`) in the meantime.
verification: CONFIRMED. Read apps/web/components/OfflineQueueProvider.tsx:99-106 (expired -> removeQueued + one critical toast), :131-141 (4xx or attempts>=MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS -> removeQueued + one critical toast) and :172-179 (flush runs on mount, on 'online', and every 30s). Read apps/web/lib/offline-queue.ts:38 (MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS=6), :50 (MAX_QUEUE_AGE_MS = 18h), :53 isExpired. Read packages/ui/src/Toast.tsx:56 — `const item = { id, durationMs: 5000, ...toast }` and OfflineQueueProvider passes no durationMs, so 5s it is. Searched apps/web for any failed/dead-letter store or review screen: none — the only stores in lib/offline-queue.ts are the single pending queue. The Monday-morning scenario follows directly from the code.

title: No timeout on any fetch — a hung API blocks every page for undici's 300 s default before failing
what: `const res = await fetch(url, init);` is issued with no `signal` / `AbortSignal.timeout`. Grepping the whole web app for `AbortSignal|AbortController|signal:` finds exactly one hit, in `app/api/readyz/route.ts` — the health check. Node 26's undici `fetch` has no default response timeout, so a server-side render blocks indefinitely; on the client every submit button stays in its `loading` state forever with no cancel.
impact: A wedged API (deadlocked Prisma pool, saturated Postgres, half-open TCP through Caddy) is strictly worse than a crashed one: the librarian gets a spinning tab that never resolves and never shows an error, so they reload, adding more hung server-side requests. There is no user-visible failure state and no server-side backpressure.
evidence: RAN: started a TCP listener on 127.0.0.1:59997 that accepts connections and never responds, pointed the production build at it, then `curl -m 45 http://127.0.0.1:3396/el/login` → `HTTP=000 time=45.006199` (curl's own cap; the request had not returned). Same code path serves every page.
fix: In `api()`, default `init.signal = AbortSignal.timeout(Number(process.env.API_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 10000))` (allow a per-request override for exports/imports), and map the resulting `TimeoutError` to a distinct, localized 'the server is not responding' state rather than letting it surface as a generic network error.
verification: PARTIALLY REFUTED. The defect is real: apps/web/lib/api.ts:103 is `const res = await fetch(url, init)` with no signal, and `grep -rn 'AbortSignal|AbortController|signal:' apps/web` returns exactly two lines, both in app/api/readyz/route.ts. But the finding's central claim — 'no default response timeout, blocks indefinitely, never shows an error' — is false, and the auditor's own curl test (capped at 45s by `-m 45`) could not have distinguished it. I measured it: a Node 26.7.0 fetch against a TCP listener that accepts and never responds threw after 301.0 s with UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT — undici's default headersTimeout is 300 s. So the real behaviour is a five-minute hang and then an error, which then hits frontend-01 and becomes a bare 500. Five minutes is still unacceptable for a page load and the fix is one line, but 'hangs forever with no error state at all' is not what happens, and a bounded-at-300s degradation under a rare half-open-upstream failure is medium, not high.

title: The moment BILLING_ENABLED is switched on, non-admin staff are locked into a dead-end screen with no sign-out and no navigation
what:
When `gate.billingEnabled && !gate.planSelected`, the layout `return`s a full-page takeover instead of the shell. For a librarian/volunteer it renders `

{libraryName}

{t('billing.choosePlanGate')}

` — a heading, a sentence, and nothing else: no sign-out, no link, no support contact. For an owner/admin it renders `ChoosePlanScreen`, which also contains no `LogoutButton` (grep for `LogoutButton|signOut|Link` in that 193-line file returns nothing). By contrast `DesktopGate.tsx:81`, the other full-page takeover, does include a `LogoutButton`.

Staff cannot sign out to let an admin sign in on the same circulation-desk machine; they must clear cookies. An admin who does not want to pick a plan yet has no way out either. Combined with `price_seed_*` placeholder price IDs, the first plan click will also fail, on a screen with no escape.
evidence:
READ: layout.tsx:117-130 — the staff branch's JSX contains only `

` and `

Also confirmed there is no GET logout route anywhere in apps/web/app — LogoutButton.tsx POSTs /auth/logout, so with no button there is genuinely no in-app way out, and /el/login would just redirect a signed-in user back to the gate. title: The desktop shell's fallback page and custom menu are English-only, and the menu bar is half-localized by Electron and half not
what: A packaged build with no `LIBRIANT_APP_URL` and no saved config loads `https://app.libriant.com`. That host has no DNS record, so `did-fail-load` fires (main.ts:270) and the shell loads `static/fallback.html`. That page is entirely hardcoded English — `<html lang="en">`, 'Can't reach Libriant', 'The app couldn't load the library server…', 'Library server URL', 'Connect' / 'Retry' / 'Open in browser', 'Desktop bridge unavailable.', 'Something went wrong.' — and it displays the raw Chromium error string (`ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`) to the user. Independently, the native menu built in main.ts:337-400 hardcodes English labels ('View', 'Connection', 'Reload from server', 'Safe mode (ignore saved server)', 'Open config folder…', 'Reset to default server', 'Check for updates…', 'Open logs…') while the adjacent `role: 'appMenu' | 'fileMenu' | 'editMenu' | 'windowMenu'` items are localized by Electron from the OS locale — so a Greek machine gets a menu bar that is half Greek, half English.
impact: The desktop app is downloaded from the tenant panel and is the paid-plan differentiator. Today every download launches straight into an English technical error demanding a URL the librarian does not know. Even after DNS is fixed, the shell's only offline/outage screen and its entire menu remain untranslated for a Greek-only customer base.
evidence: READ: config.ts:11 `export const DEFAULT_APP_URL = 'https://app.libriant.com';` (known state: this host has no DNS record). READ: main.ts:270-275 (`did-fail-load` → `loadFallback`) and static/fallback.html — every visible string is an English literal, including `errEl.textContent = (failedUrl ? failedUrl + ' — ' : '') + errText;`. READ: main.ts:352 `label: 'Connection'` and the surrounding template.
fix: Ship a bilingual fallback page (pick with `app.getLocale()`, or inline both and toggle with a `lang` query param the main process sets), translate the custom menu labels through the same locale, and either point `DEFAULT_APP_URL` at a host that resolves or bake the tenant's own URL into the installer served by `/t/:slug/desktop`.
verification: SOURCE CLAIMS CONFIRMED, FRAMING CUT BACK. Verified apps/desktop/src/config.ts:11 `export const DEFAULT_APP_URL = 'https://app.libriant.com';`, apps/desktop/static/fallback.html `<html lang="en">` with every visible string an English literal ('Can't reach Libriant', 'Library server URL', 'Connect', 'Open in browser'), and apps/desktop/src/main.ts:338-384 hardcoding 'View', 'Connection', 'Reload from server', 'Safe mode (ignore saved server)', 'Open config folder…', 'Reset to default server', 'Check for updates…', 'Open logs…' next to role-based items that Electron localizes from the OS. But the headline — 'the first screen on every fresh install is an error' — is a restatement of a KNOWN STATE the brief told us not to report as a discovery (app.libriant.com has no DNS record; nothing is deployed). Once DNS exists the fallback page is a rare screen. The durable, in-scope defect is that the desktop shell's only outage screen and its entire custom menu are English-only for a Greek-only customer base — the same class as frontend-13/15/18, hence medium.

title: No way to change language inside the app, and the tenant's own defaultLocale is never used — an en-US browser locks a Greek librarian into English permanently
where: apps/web/app/page.tsx:6-8 (only locale decision point); apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/SidebarNav.tsx (no locale control); apps/web/lib/api.ts:147 (`tenant.defaultLocale`, read but never used)
what: Locale is decided exactly once, at `/`, by `negotiateLocale(accept-language)`. `packages/i18n/src/locales.ts:25-35` returns `'en'` for any `Accept-Language` whose first supported tag is English. After that the locale is pinned in the URL prefix. The only locale switcher in the whole product is on the public landing page (`app/[locale]/page.tsx:77-84`, `.lbr-landing__locales`). There is none in the tenant shell, none on `/login`, none on `/signup`. `AuthMeResponse.tenant.defaultLocale` is typed in `lib/api.ts:147`, collected at signup (`SignupForm.tsx:112`) and displayed in the admin panel (`admin/tenants/[id]/page.tsx:270`) — but `grep -rn defaultLocale apps/web` shows it is never used to choose or redirect the locale.
impact: Greek libraries routinely run Windows/macOS in en-US. Those staff land on `/en/...`, get the whole application in English, and have no control anywhere in the UI to switch to Greek — they would have to hand-edit the URL. Anyone who bookmarks an `/en/` URL is stuck for good. The library-level language preference the product asks for at signup does nothing.
evidence: READ: app/page.tsx:6-8; packages/i18n/src/locales.ts:25-35 (`DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'el'` but any en-* Accept-Language short-circuits to 'en'). RAN: `grep -rn 'lbr-landing__locale' apps/web --include='*.tsx'` → only app/[locale]/page.tsx:77,82. RAN: `grep -rn defaultLocale apps/web` → 5 hits, none of which affect routing.
fix: Add a locale control to the tenant sidebar footer and to the auth cards (two links, same pattern as the landing page), persisting the choice in a cookie. On login, redirect to the tenant's `defaultLocale` when it differs from the URL prefix and the user has no explicit preference.
verification: CONFIRMED IN SUBSTANCE, SEVERITY CUT. Verified apps/web/app/page.tsx:6-8 (negotiateLocale on Accept-Language is the only decision point), packages/i18n/src/locales.ts:25-34 (any en-* tag short-circuits to 'en' before DEFAULT_LOCALE='el' is reached), and that the only locale switcher in apps/web is app/[locale]/page.tsx:77-84 on the public landing page. `grep -rn defaultLocale apps/web` returns 5 hits — SignupForm.tsx:112 (collected), api.ts:147 (typed), admin tenants pages (displayed) — none of which affects routing. What the finding omits, and what caps the severity: a user pinned to /en is not actually trapped. The landing page at /en carries the Ελληνικά switcher, so 'go to libriant.com, click Ελληνικά, then sign in' works, as does editing the URL prefix. That is a discoverability failure, not a lock-in. Medium.

title: The service worker serves stale API responses to online users — a newly created member is invisible on the first search after adding them
where: apps/web/public/sw.js:120 (`return cached || (await network) || Response.error();`), routed from sw.js:151-155
what: Every same-origin GET under `/lbr-api/` that is not in the `SENSITIVE` list goes through `staleWhileRevalidate`. That function returns the cached response **immediately whenever one exists** and discards the network result for the current caller, only writing it into the cache for next time. The caller has no way to observe the revalidation — there is no `clients.postMessage`, no `BroadcastChannel`, no re-render hook. So every client-side read is one round behind: `Combobox` member/book search (apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx:78), `AuthorPicker`, `DataTable.loadMore` (DataTable.tsx:110), help search, and the tenant export-status polling in `settings/export/ExportManager.tsx` all serve last-time's answer while online.
impact: At the circulation desk: add member 'Μαρία', go to checkout, type 'Μαρ' — if that exact query string was typed before she existed, the SW replays the old empty result and the picker says 'No matches'. The librarian concludes the member was not saved and creates a duplicate. The tenant export panel shows a permanently one-poll-stale job status, so a completed export appears to still be running. This is a correctness bug that only exists in production (the SW is registered only when `NODE_ENV === 'production'`, ServiceWorkerManager.tsx:17), so it will not be seen in dev or in any current test.
evidence: READ: sw.js:106-122 — `const cached = await cache.match(request); const network = fetch(request).then(...); return cached || (await network) || Response.error();`. READ: sw.js:151-155 routes all non-sensitive `/lbr-api/` GETs there. READ: ServiceWorkerManager.tsx:17 gates registration on production. (I attempted a live SW repro on a local HTTP server; service-worker registration is blocked in the audit browser, so this is a source-level determination — the control flow is unambiguous.)
fix: Use network-first (falling back to cache when offline) for `/lbr-api/` GETs instead of stale-while-revalidate. Correctness at a circulation desk matters more than the few hundred ms SWR saves, and the offline fallback is preserved either way. If SWR is kept for some endpoints, exclude all search/list endpoints and any polling endpoint.
verification: CONFIRMED at source. Read apps/web/public/sw.js:106-122: staleWhileRevalidate does `return cached || (await network) || Response.error()` and discards the network result for the current caller; :151-155 routes every non-SENSITIVE /lbr-api/ GET there. Checked the one plausible refutation — apps/web/lib/api.ts:96 sets `cache: 'no-store'` on every request — but RequestCache mode governs the HTTP cache only; it does not bypass the service worker's fetch handler, and Cache.match() does not consider it. Also confirmed the responses are same-origin (the /lbr-api rewrite), so `response.type === 'basic'` holds and they really are written to DATA_CACHE. ServiceWorkerManager.tsx:17 does gate registration on NODE_ENV==='production', so this is production-only as claimed.

title: Three simultaneously mounted Modals share id="lbr-modal-title", so the open dialog is announced with a different dialog's title
what: `Modal` hardcodes a single document-wide id for its title and points `aria-labelledby` at it. `LoanActions` renders `<ReturnModal>`, `<RenewModal>` and `<MarkLostModal>` unconditionally in the same fragment (only `open` differs), so three elements carry `id="lbr-modal-title"`. `aria-labelledby` resolves by `getElementById`, which returns the first match — the Return dialog's heading — regardless of which dialog is open. The same duplication occurs on the book detail page (BookDetail.tsx:371, 471), the member detail page, and the data-model settings page (AddFieldModal + EditFieldModal).
impact: A screen-reader user who opens 'Mark lost' hears the dialog announced as 'Return «Dune»'. On a destructive action (mark lost creates a replacement-cost charge) that is a genuine wrong-action risk, not just a nuisance. It is also invalid HTML on the highest-traffic page in the app.
evidence: RAN: served a repro reproducing LoanActions' exact structure (three `.lbr-modal` dialogs, the third `showModal()`'d) and evaluated in the browser: `document.querySelectorAll('#lbr-modal-title').length` → **3**, `document.getElementById('lbr-modal-title').textContent` → **"Επιστροφή «Dune»"** while the *Mark lost* dialog was the open one. The accessibility tree read back three separate dialogs each with its own heading, confirming all three are in the document.
fix: Generate the id per instance with `React.useId()` in `Modal` (and the same in `HelpDrawer`, which hardcodes `lbr-help-drawer-title`), and wire `aria-labelledby` to it.
verification: CONFIRMED without needing the auditor's repro. packages/ui/src/Modal.tsx:63 `aria-labelledby="lbr-modal-title"` and :74 `<h2 id="lbr-modal-title">` are hardcoded literals with no useId. apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/[id]/LoanActions.tsx:176, :185, :194 mount ReturnModal, RenewModal and MarkLostModal unconditionally in one fragment, differing only by `open`. Three elements therefore carry the same id and getElementById resolves to the first (Return). Also confirmed the same hardcoded-id bug in packages/ui/src/HelpDrawer.tsx:52/:63 ('lbr-help-drawer-title').

title: Every dismiss/close control in the design system announces an English label to Greek screen-reader users, and one of them cannot be localized at all
where: packages/ui/src/Toast.tsx:96 (`aria-label="Dismiss"`, no prop); packages/ui/src/Modal.tsx:36 (`closeLabel = 'Close'`); packages/ui/src/HelpDrawer.tsx:34 (`'Close help'`) and :90 (`'Show help for this page'`); packages/ui/src/Banner.tsx:16 (`dismissLabel = 'Dismiss'`); apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx:56-57, :84; apps/web/components/DataTable.tsx:71-74, :123
what: The UI package exposes English defaults for accessible names and, in Toast's case, no override prop at all. Grepping the app shows that **no caller ever passes `closeLabel` (12 `<Modal>` call sites), `dismissLabel` (0 call sites), or `ariaLabel` on `HelpButton` (3 tenant call sites)**. Combobox and DataTable defaults *are* overridden by their tenant callers, but their hardcoded runtime error strings are not: Combobox.tsx:84 `setError(... : 'Could not search.')` and DataTable.tsx:123 `'Something went wrong. Try again.'` are the messages shown on a network failure and have no prop.
impact: A Greek librarian using a screen reader hears 'Dismiss', 'Close', 'Close help', 'Show help for this page' throughout a Greek interface. Sighted users hit the untranslated strings too: a dropped connection while searching the catalogue shows 'Could not search.' and a failed 'load more' shows 'Something went wrong. Try again.' — in English, in the middle of Greek pages.
evidence: RAN: `grep -rn 'closeLabel' apps/web` → only the two definitions in packages/ui, zero call sites. `grep -rn 'dismissLabel' apps/web` → zero. `grep -rn '<HelpButton' apps/web/app/[locale]/t` → 3 call sites (settings/page.tsx:35, settings/support-access/page.tsx:69, catalog/page.tsx:46), none passing `ariaLabel`. Move Combobox's and DataTable's runtime error strings to required props fed from the catalogue.
verification: CONFIRMED, every claim re-run. `grep -rn closeLabel apps/web packages` -> only the definitions in Modal.tsx:16/36 and HelpDrawer.tsx:12/34; zero call sites pass it. `grep -rn dismissLabel` -> only Banner.tsx:9/16; zero call sites. packages/ui/src/Toast.tsx:96 has `aria-label="Dismiss"` with no prop at all. HelpDrawer.tsx:107 `aria-label={ariaLabel ?? 'Show help for this page'}` and none of the 8 <HelpButton> call sites passes ariaLabel. The two sighted-user strings are exactly where claimed: apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx:84 `'Could not search.'` and apps/web/components/DataTable.tsx:123 `'Something went wrong. Try again.'`.

Every string is an English literal rendered inside a document whose `<html lang>` is the URL locale: the page title `"… · Verify email"`, the heading 'Verify your email', 'Verifying your email…', 'This link is missing its token.', 'The link may have expired or already been used. Until a mail provider is configured, have the banner detect `EMAIL_DRIVER=console` (surface it from `/auth/me`) and say so, rather than claiming a mail was sent.

The invalid nesting is real: <Link> wrapping <Button> at VerifyEmailClient.tsx:60-62 and :77-79.

Read packages/ui/src/styles.css:1155-1197: .lbr-landing__hero is `linear-gradient(135deg, var(--color-primary), var(--color-accent))` with color #ffffff; .lbr-landing__eyebrow opacity .85 / --fs-sm / 600, .lbr-landing__hero-note opacity .85 / --fs-sm, .lbr-landing__hero-sub opacity .95 / clamp(1rem,2.4vw,1.25rem). Confirmed --color-warning is used as a text colour at LoansTable.tsx:81, AuditLog.tsx:97 and StaffManager.tsx:209.

title: The PWA manifest locks the app to portrait and ships SVG-only icons, so an iPad circulation desk cannot rotate and an iOS home-screen install gets no icon
where: apps/web/app/manifest.ts:21 (`orientation: 'portrait-primary'`), :24-42 (three SVG icon entries, one marked `purpose: 'maskable'`), :22 (`lang: 'en'`); apps/web/app/[locale]/layout.tsx:15 (`apple: '/_assets/brand/logo-square.svg'`)

Every declared icon is `image/svg+xml` with `sizes: 'any'`; there is no PNG anywhere in `apps/web/public` (`ls` shows only `offline.html` and `sw.js`). iOS Safari does not support SVG for `apple-touch-icon`, and the root layout points `icons.apple` at the same SVG. The manifest also declares `lang: 'en'` for a product whose default locale is `el`.
impact: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.4 Orientation (Level AA) is a straight failure: a librarian who installs the PWA on a tablet mounted in landscape at the desk — the obvious deployment for a circulation station — cannot use it in that orientation. On iPhone/iPad the home-screen tile falls back to a screenshot of the page rather than the Libriant mark, which reads as broken to a customer being onboarded. The wrong manifest `lang` mislabels the installed app.
evidence: READ: apps/web/app/manifest.ts in full; apps/web/app/[locale]/layout.tsx:12-19. RAN: `ls -la apps/web/public` → only `offline.html`, `sw.js` (no raster icons at any size). Confirmed the emitted `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/_assets/brand/logo-square.svg">` in the live HTML from the running production build.

verification: CONFIRMED, with the headline scenario corrected. apps/web/app/manifest.ts is verbatim as described: orientation 'portrait-primary' (line 21), lang 'en' (line 23), three image/svg+xml icons with sizes:'any'; `ls apps/web/public` -> only offline.html and sw.js, no raster icon at any size; app/[locale]/layout.tsx:15 points icons.apple at the SVG. CORRECTION: iOS Safari ignores the manifest `orientation` member entirely, so the finding's specific 'an iPad circulation desk cannot rotate' example is wrong — the lock bites installed PWAs on Android tablets and phones, which is where it is honoured. The SC 1.3.4 (AA) failure and the missing apple-touch-icon raster (iOS does not accept SVG there) both stand. Kept at medium on the strength of the Android orientation lock, not the iPad claim.

title: Toasts auto-dismiss after 5 s with no way to pause or recover them, and the documented hover-to-pause behaviour does not exist
what: The component's own doc comment states 'Toasts auto-dismiss after `durationMs` (default 5s) unless the user hovers over the stack (paused).' No pause exists: `show()` sets `setTimeout(() => dismiss(id), item.durationMs)` with no hover handler, no `onMouseEnter`, no timer reset, and the returned handle is explicitly discarded (`void handle`). There is no toast history and no way to bring a dismissed message back.
impact: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (Level A): a time limit on reading content with no mechanism to turn it off, adjust it, or extend it. Concretely, toasts are the only channel for several irreversible outcomes — the offline queue's 'this action was lost' messages (finding-06), the fine-created and hold-promoted details attached to a successful return, and print failures. Anyone reading Greek at normal speed, using magnification, or simply looking away misses them permanently. The false doc comment means reviewers reasonably believed the mitigation was there.
evidence: READ: Toast.tsx:36-38 (the claim) against :44-66 (`show` / `dismiss`) and :72-104 (the rendered stack) — no mouse or focus handler anywhere in the file, and the `prefers-reduced-motion` claim in the same comment is honoured only in CSS (styles.css:662-666) which disables the animation, not the timer.
fix: Implement the documented pause: track hover and focus-within on `.lbr-toast-stack` and stop/restart the timers. Set `durationMs: null` (sticky) for `severity: 'critical'` by default. Correct or delete the doc comment either way.
verification: CONFIRMED. Read packages/ui/src/Toast.tsx in full: the doc comment at :36-38 promises 'unless the user hovers over the stack (paused)', and the implementation at :55-62 is `const handle = setTimeout(() => dismiss(id), item.durationMs); void handle;` with no onMouseEnter/onFocus anywhere in the file (the rendered stack at :72-104 has no mouse or focus handler at all). No toast history exists. This directly compounds frontend-06 — the offline queue's 'this action was lost' message is a 5-second toast with no way to pause or recover it.

title: Library brand colour is accepted with no contrast check, so a library can make every primary button white-on-yellow at 1.4:1
what: The branding endpoint validates `brandColor` against `HEX` and nothing else. The chosen value is injected as `--color-primary` on `.lbr-shell`, but `--color-primary-fg` stays `#ffffff` (packages/ui/src/styles.css: `.lbr-btn--primary { background: var(--color-primary); color: var(--color-primary-fg) }`). `--color-primary` is also used as *text* on light backgrounds (`.lbr-nav__link--active`, `.lbr-toast__action`, `.lbr-landing__locale--active`). The settings form is a free `<input type="color">` with no preview warning — grepping the file for `contrast|luminance|warn` returns nothing.
impact: A library owner picking their institutional colour — yellow, light teal, light green are all common — silently makes every Save / Check out / Confirm button unreadable for every member of staff, permanently, with no warning and no automatic correction. `#ffffff` is a valid hex and yields 1.0:1, i.e. invisible buttons.
evidence: READ: branding.controller.ts:43-47 — the only check is `HEX.test(body.brandColor)`. RAN a WCAG relative-luminance computation on plausible picks against the fixed white foreground: `#ffd60a` → **1.41:1**, `#f4c542` → 1.63:1, `#4cc9f0` → 1.92:1, `#90ee90` → 1.42:1, `#ffffff` → 1.00:1 (AA requires 4.5:1 for the button label, 3:1 for the control boundary). RAN: `grep -n 'contrast|luminance|warn' BrandingForm.tsx` → no matches.
fix: Compute the contrast of the picked colour against both `#ffffff` and `#0d1117` server-side; reject (or auto-flip `--color-primary-fg` to the dark token) when the chosen pairing falls below 4.5:1, and show a live warning plus a rendered button preview in `BrandingForm` before the librarian saves.
verification: MECHANISM CONFIRMED, SEVERITY CUT. apps/api/src/branding/branding.controller.ts:43-47 really does validate only `HEX.test(body.brandColor)`; layout.tsx:184-186 injects it as --color-primary on .lbr-shell; packages/ui/src/styles.css:76-79 keeps `.lbr-btn--primary { background: var(--color-primary); color: var(--color-primary-fg) }` with --color-primary-fg fixed at white. I re-ran the luminance maths and reproduce the numbers (#ffd60a -> 1.41:1, #ffffff -> 1.00:1). But the harm is self-inflicted, immediately visible, and reversible by the same owner in the same form — they pick a colour, see the result on the next render, and can pick another. That is a missing guard-rail, not a defect that hurts someone who did nothing wrong. Low.

title: The offline page and the 404 page are English-only, and the 404 declares lang="en"
where: apps/web/public/offline.html:2 and :~230 ('You're offline', 'Try again'); apps/web/app/not-found.tsx:13 (`<html lang="en">`), :29 ('This page could not be found.'), :31 ('Go to Libriant')

You're offline

`, `

verification: CONFIRMED, SEVERITY CUT FOR CONSISTENCY. apps/web/public/offline.html line 2 is `<html lang="en">` and contains 'You're offline' / 'can't reach the network' / 'Try again'; apps/web/app/not-found.tsx:13 is `<html lang="en">` with 'This page could not be found.' and 'Go to Libriant', and it is the only not-found in the tree so it also serves locale routes. title: Critical errors are announced politely by a live region that is created at the same instant as its content, so screen readers commonly announce nothing
where: packages/ui/src/Banner.tsx:24 (`role="status" aria-live="polite"` regardless of severity); apps/web/app/[locale]/login/LoginForm.tsx:76-80 (conditionally mounted); packages/ui/src/Toast.tsx:74 (`role="region" aria-live="polite"`, unnamed)
what: `Banner` hardcodes `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` for all four severities, including `critical`. Every consumer mounts it conditionally — e.g. `{errors.form ? <Banner severity="critical">…</Banner> : null}` on the login form, and the same pattern on the loans, plans, support-access and announcement pages. A live region that is inserted into the DOM already containing its text is not reliably announced by NVDA, JAWS or VoiceOver; the region has to exist and then be mutated. There is also no focus move to the message. The toast stack is a `role="region"` with no accessible name and `aria-live="polite"` for `critical` toasts too.
impact: A screen-reader user who submits the login form with a wrong password gets, in the common case, no feedback at all: focus stays on the submit button and the error is neither spoken nor focused. The same applies to every page-level fetch error banner and every critical toast (including the offline-queue 'this action was lost' messages from finding-06).
evidence: READ: Banner.tsx:24 — `<div role="status" aria-live="polite" ...>` with no branch on `severity`. READ: LoginForm.tsx:76-80 — the Banner is rendered only when `errors.form` is set, i.e. node and text appear together; `handleSubmit` (line 63-70) sets the error and never moves focus. READ: Toast.tsx:74.
fix: Use `role="alert"` (implicit `aria-live="assertive"`) for `severity="critical"` in `Banner`, keep `status` for the rest. Render a permanently-mounted, empty live region in the auth card and the tenant shell and write the message into it, rather than mounting the region with the message. Move focus to the error banner (`tabIndex={-1}` + `.focus()`) after a failed submit. Give the toast stack an `aria-label` and use `role="alert"` on individual critical toasts.
verification: PARTLY REFUTED. The code is as described: packages/ui/src/Banner.tsx:24 hardcodes `role="status" aria-live="polite"` with no branch on severity; LoginForm.tsx:76-80 mounts the Banner only when errors.form is set and handleSubmit (:64-71) never moves focus; Toast.tsx:74 is an unnamed role="region". But the impact does not follow as stated. 'A live region inserted with its content is not announced' is folklore that modern NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver frequently contradict — behaviour is AT- and version-dependent, and the auditor did not test with any screen reader (proved_by: read-only, confidence: medium, by their own admission). WCAG-wise there is no clear failure either: SC 4.1.3 Status Messages is satisfied by role=status. What remains is genuine but minor — critical severity should map to role="alert", and a failed submit should move focus. Low.

title: The sidebar's Billing item is a hardcoded English string with no catalogue key — it appears the moment subscriptions are enabled
what: `...(isAdmin && billingEnabled ? [{ href: \`${base}/billing\`, label: 'Billing' }] : [])` — every other entry in the `links` array uses `t('common.nav.*')`. There is no `nav.billing` key in either catalogue: `locales/el/common.json` contains `nav.catalog, nav.members, nav.loans, nav.reservations, nav.settings, nav.staff, nav.help, nav.language, nav.menu, nav.closeMenu, nav.desktop` and nothing else.
impact: The item is hidden today because `billingEnabled` is false, so this is invisible in every current test and every screenshot. The moment `BILLING_ENABLED=true` is set, the Greek sidebar grows an English 'Billing' row next to Κατάλογος / Μέλη / Δανεισμοί. The translation-parity CI gate cannot catch it, because the key does not exist in either language.
evidence: READ: SidebarNav.tsx:89. RAN: `python3 -c "import json; print(list(json.load(open('locales/el/common.json')).keys()))"` → no `nav.billing`. RAN the repo-wide key-usage cross-check (792 distinct `t('...')` keys against 1027 catalogue keys): zero missing keys — because this string never goes through `t()` at all, which is exactly why the existing gate misses it.
fix: Add `nav.billing` to `locales/en/common.json` and `locales/el/common.json` and use `t('common.nav.billing')`. Extend `scripts/check-translations.ts` (which today only checks en/el key parity) with a lint rule that flags string literals in JSX text and `label`/`title`/`aria-label`/`placeholder` props inside `apps/web/app/[locale]/t` and `packages/ui` — that scan found 23 such literals in tenant-facing code.
verification: CONFIRMED, SEVERITY CUT. SidebarNav.tsx:89 is verbatim `...(isAdmin && billingEnabled ? [{ href: `${base}/billing`, label: 'Billing' }] : [])`, and every sibling at :82-93 uses t('common.nav.*'). Dumped locales/el/common.json: nav keys are catalog, members, loans, reservations, settings, staff, help, language, menu, closeMenu, desktop — no nav.billing in either catalogue, so the parity gate genuinely cannot see it. All true, and the observation about why the CI gate misses it is the useful part. But the defect itself is one English word in one dormant, admin-only sidebar row. Low.

title: FormField marks fields required visually only — the input carries no required/aria-required
what: The `required` prop renders `*` — correctly hidden from assistive tech — but the `React.cloneElement` call that injects `id`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` into the child does not inject `required` or `aria-required`. So the only signal that a field is mandatory is an asterisk explicitly hidden from screen readers.
impact: Screen-reader users filling in signup, checkout, new member or new book forms cannot tell which fields are mandatory until submission fails — and, per finding-20, the failure is frequently not announced either. WCAG 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions.
evidence: READ: FormField.tsx:59-71. The `cloneElement` props object is `{ id, 'aria-describedby': describedBy, 'aria-invalid': ..., invalid: ... }` — no `required`.
fix: Add `'aria-required': required || undefined` to the cloned props (prefer `aria-required` over the native `required` attribute so browser-native validation bubbles do not fight the app's own `noValidate` handling).
verification: CONFIRMED. packages/ui/src/FormField.tsx:58-63 renders the asterisk inside `<span aria-hidden="true">`, and the cloneElement props object at :65-70 is exactly `{ id, 'aria-describedby', 'aria-invalid', invalid }` — no required, no aria-required. So the mandatory-field signal is the one thing explicitly hidden from assistive tech.

title: Every modal injects a spurious banner and contentinfo landmark, so a loan detail page reports three page headers and three footers
what: `<header>` and `<footer>` map to the `banner` and `contentinfo` landmarks unless they are scoped inside `article`, `aside`, `main`, `nav` or `section`. `<dialog>` is not in that list, so both elements inside a Modal become top-level landmarks. Because `LoanActions` mounts three Modals at once (see finding-12), a loan detail page contains three `banner` landmarks and three `contentinfo` landmarks in addition to the shell's own.
impact: Landmark navigation — a primary screen-reader way to move around a page — becomes useless on the busiest pages: 'banner' should be a unique, page-level region and instead lists four indistinguishable entries. Not blocking, but it degrades the same users already hurt by findings 12, 13 and 14.
evidence: RAN: rendered the Modal markup in the browser and read the accessibility tree, which reported `dialog > banner > heading` for each of the three dialogs — the `<header>` is exposed as a `banner` landmark, confirmed by the tool's own tree output.
fix: Replace `<header>`/`<footer>` inside `Modal` and `HelpDrawer` with `<div>`s (the class names already carry all the styling), or wrap the dialog's contents in a `<section>`.
verification: CONFIRMED on the spec, which is the load-bearing part. packages/ui/src/Modal.tsx:70 `<header className="lbr-modal__header">` and :85 `<footer className="lbr-modal__actions">`; HelpDrawer.tsx:60 the same. Per HTML-AAM, header/footer map to banner/contentinfo unless scoped inside article, aside, main, nav or section (or the equivalent roles); <dialog> maps to role=dialog and is not in that list, so the mapping to banner/contentinfo applies. Combined with the three-modals-mounted-at-once fact independently confirmed under frontend-12, a loan detail page really does carry four banner landmarks. Low is the right weight — landmark clutter, no functional loss.

title: Combobox reports an expanded listbox that does not exist, points aria-controls at a missing id, and puts a role=alert li inside a listbox
what: `aria-expanded={open}` is bound to the `open` state alone, but the `<ul role="listbox">` is rendered only when `open && query.trim().length >= minQueryChars` — so focusing the input with an empty query reports 'expanded' with no popup present, and `aria-controls={listboxId}` dangles. Inside the listbox, the loading, error and no-matches rows are `<li>` elements without `role="option"`, and the error row additionally carries `role="alert"` — neither is a permitted child of `role="listbox"`. There is also no live region reporting how many results were found.
impact: The member and book pickers in checkout and place-hold are the two most-used custom widgets in the product. A screen-reader user is told a list is open when it is not, is given no result count, and encounters children the listbox role does not permit — behaviour varies by AT but is wrong everywhere.
evidence:
READ: Combobox.tsx:150-153 (`aria-expanded={open}` / `aria-controls={listboxId}`) against :157 (`{open && query.trim().length >= minQueryChars ?
    `), and :168-171 (`
  • {error}
    • `).
fix: Bind `aria-expanded` to the same condition that renders the listbox. Render the loading/error/empty rows outside the `<ul>` (in a sibling `<div role="status">` that also announces the result count), leaving the listbox containing only `role="option"` children.
verification: CONFIRMED verbatim. apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx:160 `aria-expanded={open}` and :161 `aria-controls={listboxId}` against :164 `{open && query.trim().length >= minQueryChars ? <ul id={listboxId} role="listbox">` — so an empty focused input reports expanded with a dangling aria-controls. Inside the listbox, :166-176 render loading / error / no-matches as plain `<li className="lbr-combobox__option--inert">` with no role=option, and the error one carries role="alert" — neither is a permitted child of role=listbox.

title: Footer legal links are 17 px tall on mobile, under the WCAG 2.2 minimum target size, and the coarse-pointer rule does not cover them
where: packages/ui/src/styles.css:1448-1462 (`@media (pointer: coarse)` list) and the `.lbr-legal-links__item` / `.lbr-powered-by` rules
what: The coarse-pointer block enlarges `.lbr-btn`, `.lbr-nav__link`, `.lbr-modal__close`, `.lbr-help-drawer__close`, `.lbr-banner__dismiss`, `.lbr-toast__close`, `.lbr-toast__action`, `.lbr-combobox__clear` and `.lbr-help-button` to 44 px, but not `.lbr-legal-links__item` or `.lbr-powered-by`. `.lbr-legal-links` uses `gap: var(--sp-1) var(--sp-3)`, i.e. 4 px of vertical spacing, so the spacing exception in SC 2.5.8 does not rescue them.
impact: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), Level AA — 24×24 CSS px. Measured targets are 17 px tall. These are the Terms, Privacy, Cookies and Legal Notice links required by the GDPR/consent work, so they are the links a regulator or a user with a motor impairment is most likely to try to tap.
evidence: RAN: loaded `/el` from the production build at 375×812 (mobile preset, touch emulation) and audited every focusable element's bounding box. Under-24 px results: `A.lbr-powered-by 184x16`, `A.lbr-legal-links__item 86x17 "Όροι Χρήσης"`, `132x17 "Πολιτική Απορρήτου"`, `112x17 "Πολιτική Cookies"`, `115x17 "Νομική Σημείωση"`. No other element failed, and `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` was exactly 375 with zero horizontally-overflowing elements — the responsive layer itself is sound.
fix: Add `.lbr-legal-links__item` and `.lbr-powered-by` to the `@media (pointer: coarse)` block with `min-height: 44px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center`, or raise the vertical gap on `.lbr-legal-links` to 24 px so the spacing exception applies.
verification: CONFIRMED at source (I did not re-run the browser measurement, but the CSS makes the result deterministic). packages/ui/src/styles.css:1447-1464 is the `@media (pointer: coarse)` block and its selector list is exactly .lbr-btn, .lbr-nav__link, .lbr-modal__close, .lbr-help-drawer__close, .lbr-banner__dismiss, .lbr-toast__close, .lbr-toast__action, .lbr-combobox__clear, .lbr-help-button — .lbr-legal-links__item and .lbr-powered-by are absent. :1558-1568 gives .lbr-legal-links `gap: var(--sp-1) var(--sp-3)` (4px row gap) and .lbr-legal-links__item `font-size: var(--fs-sm)` with no padding or min-height, so the target box is the ~17px line box the auditor measured, and the 4px row gap rules out the SC 2.5.8 spacing exception. The inline-in-a-sentence exception does not apply either — these are flex items, not running text.

title: The static cache version is pinned to v1, so it is never invalidated and grows across every deploy
what: `STATIC_CACHE = \`lbr-static-${VERSION}\`` with a literal `'v1'` that nothing bumps. The `activate` handler deletes only `lbr-` caches not in `ALL_CACHES`, and `ALL_CACHES` always contains the same three names, so nothing is ever evicted. `isImmutableAsset` sends every `/_next/static/*` chunk and every path ending in a static extension to `cacheFirst`, which writes and never expires. Over successive deploys the cache accumulates one full set of hashed chunks per release. `offline.html` is also precached into this never-cleared cache (sw.js:66), so a corrected offline page will not reach a browser that already installed the old one.
impact: Unbounded storage growth on long-lived circulation-desk browsers, and — more awkwardly — a fix to `offline.html` (see finding-18) will not actually ship to existing installs, because `cache.add(OFFLINE_URL)` only runs on install and `caches.match(OFFLINE_URL)` prefers the stale entry. Not urgent on day one; it becomes a support problem after a few releases.
evidence: READ: sw.js:19, 22-30, 62-72, 77-83, 95-104. `VERSION` appears exactly once and is a literal.
fix: Derive `VERSION` from the build id (inject it by generating `sw.js` at build time from a template, or append `?v=<buildId>` to the registration URL and read it in the worker) so each deploy gets fresh cache names and the activate handler evicts the previous set. Fetch `offline.html` with `cache: 'reload'` in the install step.
verification: CONFIRMED, and one implication is stronger than the finding states. apps/web/public/sw.js:19 `const VERSION = 'v1'` appears exactly once and is a literal; :77-83 activate deletes only lbr-* caches absent from ALL_CACHES, which is always the same three names. Additional point I verified: sw.js is a static file in /public that is byte-identical between deploys, so the browser sees no byte change and never even re-installs the worker — which means `cache.add(OFFLINE_URL)` at :66 never re-runs and a corrected offline.html genuinely cannot reach an existing install. Low: storage growth is slow and nothing breaks on day one.

title: The offline bar, the pending-queue pill and the toast stack all occupy the bottom-right corner and none respects the iOS safe area
where: apps/web/components/ServiceWorkerManager.tsx:33-45 (full-width bottom bar, z-index 2000); apps/web/components/OfflineQueueProvider.tsx:200-218 (bottom-right pill, z-index 1900); packages/ui/src/styles.css `.lbr-toast-stack` (bottom-right, z-index 9000, no safe-area padding)
what: Three fixed overlays anchor to the bottom of the viewport. When the device is offline with queued actions — the exact state the offline feature exists for — the pending pill (z-index 1900) sits underneath the full-width offline bar (z-index 2000), and any toast (z-index 9000) covers both. Only the offline bar and the pill add `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`; `.lbr-toast-stack` uses a plain `bottom: var(--sp-5)`.
impact: On a phone or an iPad at the desk, the '3 actions pending' indicator is obscured by the offline banner precisely when the librarian needs to know whether their checkouts are queued. On a notched iPhone the toast close button can land under the home indicator and be hard to tap.
evidence: READ: ServiceWorkerManager.tsx:33-45 (`position:'fixed', left:0, right:0, bottom:0, zIndex:2000`, `paddingBottom: calc(... + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))`); OfflineQueueProvider.tsx:200-218 (`right`/`bottom: calc(var(--sp-3) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))`, `zIndex:1900`); styles.css `.lbr-toast-stack { bottom: var(--sp-5); right: var(--sp-5); z-index: 9000 }` — no `env()`.
fix: Stack the three in one bottom-anchored flow container rather than overlapping fixed layers, or raise the queue pill above the offline bar and offset it by the bar's height when both are shown. Add `bottom: calc(var(--sp-5) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))` to `.lbr-toast-stack`.
verification: CONFIRMED. apps/web/components/ServiceWorkerManager.tsx:33-45 — position fixed, left:0 right:0 bottom:0, zIndex 2000, with env(safe-area-inset-bottom). apps/web/components/OfflineQueueProvider.tsx:200-218 — position fixed, right var(--sp-3), bottom calc(var(--sp-3) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)), zIndex 1900. The pill sits ~12px off the bottom edge with a lower z-index than a full-width bar that starts at bottom:0 and is taller than that, so it is fully covered whenever both show — which is exactly the offline-with-queued-actions state. packages/ui/src/styles.css:591 `.lbr-toast-stack { bottom: var(--sp-5) }` with no env() — confirmed.

title: There is not a single frontend test in the repository — 172 TS/TSX files across the web app and UI package have zero coverage
where: apps/web/ and packages/ui/ (no *.test.* / *.spec.* files; the only test runner config is apps/api/vitest.config.ts)
what: `find apps/web packages/ui -name '*.test.*' -o -name '*.spec.*'` returns nothing, and `find apps -name 'vitest.config*' -o -name 'jest.config*'` returns only the API's. `packages/ui/package.json` has no `test` script (`lint` is literally `echo 'lint: ok (no lint configured yet)'`). There is no jsdom/Testing Library dependency and no axe or Lighthouse gate in CI.
impact: Not a defect in itself, but it is the mechanism behind most of the findings above: duplicate DOM ids, English defaults never overridden at 20+ call sites, a toast rendered under a top-layer dialog, a doc comment describing behaviour that was never implemented, and a plan-gate screen with no way out are all things a single render test or an axe assertion would have caught. It also means none of the fixes above can be regression-protected as things stand.
evidence: RAN: `find apps/web packages/ui -name '*.test.*' -o -name '*.spec.*' | grep -v node_modules` → empty. RAN: `find apps -name 'vitest.config*' -o -name 'jest.config*'` → `apps/api/vitest.config.ts` only. READ: packages/ui/package.json (no test script, no test deps).
fix: Add vitest + @testing-library/react + jest-axe to `packages/ui` and `apps/web` and start with the cheapest high-value set: an axe pass over each design-system component, a test asserting Modal ids are unique when several are mounted, and a render test per full-page takeover (`ChoosePlanScreen`, the staff plan gate, `SystemModeTakeover`) asserting a sign-out control is present.
verification: CONFIRMED. `find apps/web packages/ui -name '*.test.*' -o -name '*.spec.*'` (excluding node_modules) returns nothing; the only runner config under apps/ is apps/api/vitest.config.ts. Correctly filed as info — it is context for the other findings, not a defect on its own.
